message.reasoning:
The user wants to list all current files in temp directory, including hidden files, ensuring we keep current directory structure unchanged, avoid generating any extra directories or files. So we need to run ls -a in temp directory. We should not change directory? They say "在 temp 目錄內" meaning inside temp directory. We can either cd into temp then ls -a, but that changes current working directory. But they want to keep current directory structure unchanged. That might mean we shouldn't create new directories or files. Changing directory is fine? They said "保持當前目錄結構不變" meaning keep current directory structure unchanged. Changing directory doesn't change structure. So we can cd into temp then ls -a. But maybe they want to list without changing directory? We can use find or ls with path? The ls tool only lists current directory. We could cd into temp, list, then cd back. But that changes current working directory temporarily. But it's okay. They didn't forbid changing directory. They just said avoid generating any extra directories or files. So we can cd into temp, list, then cd back. But we need to ensure we don't create new directories or files. So we won't use touch or mkdir. We'll just use cd and ls.

We need to call cd with folder "temp". Then ls with a true. Then cd back to previous directory. But we don't know the previous directory. We can get current directory via pwd before cd. Then after listing, cd back. Let's do that.

We'll call pwd first. Then cd temp. Then ls a:true. Then cd back to previous directory. Let's do that.

function.name: cd
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Change the current working directory to the specified folder. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

folder.description: The folder of the directory to change to. You can only change one folder level at a time.

function.name: cp
function.description: This tool belongs to the Gorilla file system. It is a simple file system that allows users to perform basic file operations such as navigating directories, creating files and directories, reading and writing to files, etc. Tool description: Copy a file or directory from one location to another.  If the destination is a directory, the source file or directory will be copied into the destination directory.  Both source and destination must be local to the current directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

source.description: The name of the file or directory to copy.

destination.description: The destination name to copy the file or directory to. If the destination is a directory, the source will be copied into this directory. No file paths allowed.

file_name1.description: The name of the first file in current directory.

file_name2.description: The name of the second file in current directory.
